# axual_group (Resource)

Group resource. Read more: https://docs.axual.io/axual/2026.1/self-service/user-group-management.html#groups

## Platform Manager version

- A service account as a member or a manager needs Platform Manager 16.0.0 or later. Users work
  with every supported version.

## Required Roles
- TENANT_ADMIN

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Group's name

### Optional

- `email_address` (String) Group's email address
- `iam_reference` (String) The group's value in your identity system, as it is in the token (for example an Azure AD group object id). Setting it makes the group IAM-managed: the identity system decides who is a member. Removing it makes the group Axual-managed again. Must be unique in the tenant. See the guide "IAM-managed groups".
- `managers` (Set of String) A Group Manager can edit this group, including adding or removing users and other group managers. Each entry is the uid of a user or of a service account, and must also be listed in `members`. Cannot be set when `iam_reference` is set. Read more: https://docs.axual.io/axual/2026.1/self-service/user-group-management.html#making-a-group-member-manager-of-the-group
- `members` (Set of String) Group's members. Each entry is the uid of a user or of a service account. Adding a service account requires Tenant Admin; once it is a member, a group manager may promote or remove it. Cannot be set when `iam_reference` is set.
- `phone_number` (String) Group's phone number

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Group's unique identifier

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "axual_group" "team-awesome" {
  name          = "Team Awesome"
  phone_number="+37253412559"
  email_address="team.awesome@example.com"
  members       = [
    	data.axual_user.tom.id,
    	data.axual_user.john.id
    	]
  managers       = [
      	data.axual_user.tom.id,
      	data.axual_user.john.id
      	]
}
```

## IAM-managed groups

Set `iam_reference` to let your identity system decide who is a member of the group. Leave out `members` and `managers`: the plan refuses them when `iam_reference` is set. The guide [IAM-managed groups](../guides/iam-managed-groups.md) explains linking, unlinking, import and service accounts.

```hcl
resource "axual_group" "payments" {
  name          = "Payments Team"
  email_address = "payments@example.com"
  iam_reference = "payments-team"
}
```

- A Tenant Admin has to switch on IAM group management for the tenant. The provider does not change these settings.
- Removing `iam_reference` makes the group Axual-managed again. The members and managers that Platform Manager has stored count again, and the next plan shows them.
- A group that is already linked outside Terraform, for example in Self-Service, is planned to be unlinked until you add its `iam_reference`.
- People who are members only through their token cannot yet create applications, topics or environments for the group, and cannot save an application in Self-Service. These are Platform Manager problems.

For a full example which shows the capabilities of the latest TerraForm provider, check https://github.com/Axual/terraform-provider-axual/tree/master/examples/axual.

## Import

Import is supported by ID, or by name (`name:`):

```shell
terraform import axual_group.<LOCAL NAME> <GROUP UID>
terraform import axual_group.test_group b21cf1d63a55436391463cee3f56e393
terraform import axual_group.<LOCAL NAME> name:<GROUP NAME>
terraform import axual_group.test_group 'name:Team Payments'
```

The name must match exactly, case included. An `import` block (Terraform 1.5 or later) takes the same IDs:

```terraform
import {
  to = axual_group.test_group
  id = "name:Team Payments"
}
```

In Terraform 1.12 or later, an `import` block can use `identity` instead of `id`:

```terraform
import {
  to = axual_group.example
  identity = {
    id = "b21cf1d63a55436391463cee3f56e393"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The ID used to import this resource.
